territorial_scope.description: State-level Washington law; protects Washington residents as consumers, with residency presumed from location in Washington state.

evidence.quote: "Consumer" means a natural person who is a Washington resident

summary.short: Introduced Washington bill that would require retail grocery sellers to post prices clearly, prohibit surveillance-based price discrimination and surge pricing, and bar electronic shelf label systems in retail locations of 15,000 square feet or larger until January 1, 2030, with a state study due June 30, 2029.
summary.long: State bill (introduced, pending) covering algorithmic and AI-based pricing of retail goods. Section 3 requires a person engaged in retail sale of goods to clearly post prices in a retail location, and prohibits surveillance-based price discrimination (setting or modifying a consumer's price from monitoring, tracking or automated analysis of behavior, location, demographics or personal information) and surge pricing (price increases based on demand, consumer behavior or willingness to pay rather than actual costs). Uniform price reductions for eligible consumers and certain loyalty programs are excepted where personal information is not used to modify prices. Section 4 bars use of electronic shelf label systems in retail locations of 15,000 square feet or larger until January 1, 2030, and expires June 30, 2031. Section 5 declares violations an unfair or deceptive act and unfair method of competition under the Consumer Protection Act, chapter 19.86 RCW. Section 2 defines key terms, including Consumer (a Washington resident) and Person (a business in retail sale of goods, excluding small businesses under RCW 19.85.020). Section 8 directs the department to study electronic shelf label systems and their impact on pricing transparency and employee job security, with a report due by June 30, 2029; that section also expires June 30, 2031.

relations.note: The definition of 'Goods' refers to the definition of 'grocery establishment' in RCW 49.85.015.
The 'Person' definition excludes a 'small business' as defined in RCW 19.85.020.
The 'Education information' category of personally identifiable information is defined by reference to 20 U.S.C. Sec. 1232g as it existed on December 18, 2025.

Sec. 5 provides that the practices covered by the chapter are matters vitally affecting the public interest for the purpose of applying the consumer protection act, and that a violation is an unfair or deceptive act and an unfair method of competition under that act.

notes: Bill text as introduced. No enabling act (legal_basis) is stated. Secs. 2 to 6 are stated to constitute a new chapter in Title 19 RCW (Sec. 7), with no existing instrument named as target. Sec. 4(1) bars use of electronic shelf label systems in retail locations of 15,000 square feet or larger until January 1, 2030, while Sec. 4(2) and Sec. 8(2) set expiry at June 30, 2031; the Sec. 1 findings describe a four-year moratorium. The title refers to expiration dates, but only Secs. 4 and 8 state them. Sec. 8 applies the Sec. 2 definition of electronic shelf label system inside chapter 43.330 RCW, while Sec. 2 definitions apply only throughout the new chapter. Source typos: 'ules' (Sec. 2(1)), 'Surveillance pricin' (Sec. 2(12)), '43.330RCW' (Sec. 8).
